title: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud
content:
OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud
OpenAI and Google Cloud(opens in a new window) are partnering to bring OpenAI’s frontier models and Codex(opens in a new window) agentic workflows into Google Cloud’s Model Garden. The integration will give customers native access to these models to power complex agentic workflows at scale, backed by Google Cloud’s data governance and high-performance infrastructure.
Google Cloud’s longstanding investment in machine learning and AI has made it a destination for AI workloads and the developers and data scientists building them. Bringing OpenAI models to its model garden gives these teams access to OpenAI’s frontier models within the environment where they already work, enabling enterprises to modernize their software development lifecycle, build agentic workflows, and change how people work.
For organizations in regulated industries, deploying AI requires control over who can access sensitive data and how it is used. The integration will pair OpenAI’s frontier models with Google Cloud’s built-in access controls, centralized data governance, and high-performance infrastructure to support demanding enterprise workloads.
Google Cloud customers will be able to purchase OpenAI frontier models via model garden, transacted through the Google Cloud Marketplace. Enterprises with Google Cloud spend commitments will be able to draw down their GCP commitments for these purchases.
Additionally, OpenAI models will soon be available in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent, providing enterprise customers with model choice flexibility and the best model for each task. By expanding access through Google Cloud, we are giving enterprises greater choice in how they discover and use frontier models, with a path from evaluation to broader adoption.
General availability is planned in the coming weeks. Request access to OpenAI on Google Cloud here.
Microsoft remains OpenAI’s primary cloud partner.

report.summary: OpenAI will bring its frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud’s Model Garden, letting enterprises access them under Google governance and billing.
report.background: OpenAI has historically relied on Microsoft Azure as its primary cloud partner, but this deal shows it pursuing a multi-cloud distribution strategy as enterprise demand for model choice grows. Google Cloud has invested heavily in AI infrastructure and its Model Garden, a catalog where customers can discover and use third-party and Google models within one governed environment. Enterprises, especially in regulated industries, want frontier AI without moving sensitive data or losing access controls, and many already have committed Google Cloud spending. By adding OpenAI models, Google Cloud strengthens its position as an enterprise AI hub while OpenAI gains a new channel into Google-centric customers. The partnership also reflects a broader shift: cloud providers are becoming neutral model marketplaces, not just exclusive model hosts.
key_points: OpenAI’s frontier models and Codex agentic workflows will be available natively in Google Cloud’s Model Garden. Customers can use them inside the Google Cloud environment they already rely on, backed by Google Cloud’s data governance and high-performance infrastructure for demanding enterprise workloads.

Enterprises will be able to buy OpenAI models through the Google Cloud Marketplace and apply existing Google Cloud spending commitments to those purchases. This reduces procurement friction and makes it easier for organizations already invested in Google Cloud to adopt OpenAI models from evaluation to broader production deployment.

The integration targets regulated industries by pairing OpenAI models with Google Cloud access controls and centralized data governance. That matters for organizations that need to control who can access sensitive data and how it is used while still adopting frontier AI and agentic workflows at scale.

OpenAI models will also soon appear in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent, giving customers more model-choice flexibility. General availability is planned in the coming weeks, and Microsoft remains OpenAI’s primary cloud partner, signaling expansion rather than replacement.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is a notable step toward multi-cloud model distribution: OpenAI models will sit alongside Google’s own models inside a rival cloud, and cloud providers increasingly act as neutral marketplaces. For developers, it lowers procurement and security hurdles, making it easier to evaluate OpenAI models within Google Cloud governance and build agentic workflows without switching environments. It may also simplify billing for teams with GCP commitments, though they will still need to manage model choice, cost, and data controls across providers. For regular users, the practical effect is likely indirect: more enterprise AI products and internal tools may ship faster, with stronger governance, as companies gain flexibility to choose the best model for each task.
report.tools: Watch Google Cloud Model Garden and Vertex AI for access and governance features; OpenAI Codex for agentic coding workflows; and Google Antigravity and Gemini Agent for model-choice experimentation. For open-source follow-up, LiteLLM can unify multiple model APIs, while LangGraph or CrewAI help prototype agentic workflows before production.
